Which Sherburne County offices deal with my tax bill?

Two departments handle it, and they share one suite in Elk River. Valuation and classification belong to the Assessor (763-765-4900). Billing and collection belong to the Auditor/Treasurer (763-765-4350). The street address for both is 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668.

The Auditor/Treasurer works out tax rates, prepares statements and the "truth in taxation" notices, and tracks every levy from towns, cities and schools. When a parcel falls behind, that same department takes judgment and starts forfeiture under state law. Think of the Assessor as the office for arguing about worth, and the Auditor/Treasurer as the office for learning what you owe on the day you list the house.

Housing in Sherburne County

Sherburne sits in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro area, with Elk River as the seat and biggest city. Population reached 104,194 in July 2025, up 7.2% from April 2020. Owners live in 83.2% of occupied homes, and a typical owned home is worth $361,400. Renters pay about $1,127 a month. Lakes, rivers and the Sherburne National Wildlife Refuge all lie within the county, so setting can move a parcel's value as much as the house does.

The county holds 38,457 housing units across 35,555 occupied homes, and the usual household brings in $105,466 a year. Builders pulled 319 permits in 2025, so new construction is a steady source of competition for resale listings.

Due dates and penalties

Mark May 15 and October 15. Farmland owners get until November 15 for the second half. The county counts a mailed check as on time only if the postmark falls on or before the deadline, and many post offices now stamp mail two or three days after pickup. A real estate bill of $50 or less has just one deadline, May 15. This year's October 15 date is behind us, so check that the second half posted before you list.

Penalties begin the day after each deadline and rise month by month. This is the schedule for a first half left unpaid:

First-half penalty by date, 2026
Date reachedHomestead or cabinNon-homestead
May 162%4%
June 14%8%
July 15%9%
October 18%12%
January 2 of the following year10%14%

An unpaid second half starts at 2% for homesteads and 4% for everything else on October 16. Farm homesteads that miss the November deadline owe 6%, and non-homestead farmland owes 8%. Owners paying late should ask the property tax division for the exact penalty before sending money.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sherburne County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to pay Sherburne County tax

The county's payment page lays out five routes. Checks go to the Sherburne County Auditor / Treasurer at the Elk River address. The property tax division in the Government Center also takes cash or check at the counter, and a drop box by the main entrance (door A) stays open after hours.

  • Forte, online or at 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307: 2.40% of the tax (minimum $2.00) on credit cards, $1.55 per eCheck, $4.00 on a debit card. Keep the parcel ID handy.
  • Direct payment: withdrawals on May 15 and October 15, or November 15 for farmland. Forms must arrive by April 15 for the spring withdrawal and September 15 for the fall one, and a cancellation has to meet those same cutoffs.
  • Lender escrow: if your mortgage payment includes tax, the lender sends it. Confirm with your servicer.

A withdrawal that lands on a weekend or bank holiday happens the following business day.

How can I contest a Sherburne County value or class?

Gather evidence first, such as a recent appraisal or sales of similar homes, and talk it over with the Assessor. If that does not settle things, attend the local board shown on your valuation notice. Local boards meet at the city or township hall in April, and the exact date is printed on the notice. Next spring's notice will carry the new dates.

  • Local board: April, at the city or township hall.
  • County board: held on a Tuesday in June at 3:00 p.m. (June 16 in 2026), by appointment only, arranged through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351.
  • Minnesota Tax Court: you may petition directly after receiving the notice, up to April 30 of the year the tax is payable (court phone 651-296-2806).

The Assessor also runs an online tool at gis.co.sherburne.mn.us/AssessmentSchedule that shows the year an appraiser will inspect an address, since every property needs a physical review once in five years.

Minnesota statutes call for estimated market value to sit at 100% of market, so appraisers review current sales continuously and note any physical change that affects land or buildings. A new deck, a finished basement or a demolished garage all belong in the conversation, because they alter what the appraiser should have on file.

Errors discovered afterward can be corrected through an abatement request to the Assessor. The county lists three kinds: homestead (you must show you lived there), valuation and classification, and a local option for a house where disaster damage reaches half the structure's value. Pay on schedule meanwhile, because review can take months.

Before you list: a short checklist

  1. Call the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4350 and ask for the balance on both halves, plus any penalty already running.
  2. Print your current statement and valuation notice. A buyer or title company will ask for the parcel figures.
  3. Check with the Assessor at 763-765-4900 whether the class on file matches how the house is used today, since a homestead that has become a rental is taxed differently.
  4. If you made changes such as a deck or a finished basement, tell the Assessor so the record is accurate before the next notice goes out.
  5. If your mortgage payment includes tax, ask the servicer what sits in escrow and when it will be refunded after closing.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sherburne County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Sherburne County home

Any unpaid balance gets cleared at the closing table, normally out of your proceeds. Phone the Auditor/Treasurer for the amount due on the parcel, and ask your lender what sits in escrow if one collects your tax. If you are selling for cash, the same payoff figure applies, and you can have it in hand before an offer arrives.

Selling a homesteaded house also creates a duty. Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), requires you to report the sale, transfer or change of primary residence to the Assessor within 30 days. An online change-of-address form is posted on the county site. Request a copy of the current statement from the Auditor/Treasurer too, as the title company will want the parcel figures.

Frequently asked questions

Which dates should I remember for Sherburne County real estate tax?

May 15 and October 15, with agricultural parcels paying the second half on November 15. A bill of $50 or less is entirely due May 15. Postmarks decide whether a mailed check is on time.

What is the Sherburne County Assessor's phone number?

763-765-4900. The office works from 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, and it deals with value, class, abatements and the opening stage of any appeal.

Does Sherburne County accept credit cards for tax?

Yes, through Forte online or by calling 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307. Expect 2.40% on credit cards with a $2.00 floor, $1.55 on eChecks and $4.00 on debit cards, shown before you confirm.

Where does a county board of appeal hearing take place in Sherburne County?

At the Sherburne County Government Center in Elk River. Owners still unhappy after their local board must book through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351.

What must I report after selling my Sherburne County homestead?

Tell the Assessor within 30 days, as Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), requires. Call 763-765-4900 with questions.

Chisago County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Chisago County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Which office bills property tax

The Auditor-Treasurer's Office in Center City calculates, bills and collects every property tax bill in Chisago County. It sits at 313 N Main Street, Room 271/274, and answers at 651-213-8500 from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday except holidays. Center City is also the county seat.

The same office handles property combinations and splits, records land transfers so names and addresses stay current, tracks special assessments, runs the tax forfeiture process and settles collected money with the local governments. Homestead applications and valuation questions go to the county assessor instead.

When statements arrive

Real estate statements go out by March 31, and manufactured home statements by July 15. They also appear online one to two weeks after mailing. The statement is the only notice you get, and its two bottom stubs carry the first-half and second-half due dates.

Statement files are generated in mid-February for the owner of record at that moment. Anyone who bought later receives no statement, and the county still holds the owner responsible for knowing when taxes are due. Download a copy from the county's property tax page or call for one. Statements go to the owner whether or not a mortgage escrow account exists, so find out whether the lender or you pay.

Due dates

Tax under $100 and all personal property is due in full on May 15. Larger bills may be paid in two installments, and the dates depend on the property class.

  • Real estate: May 15 and October 15
  • Agricultural: May 15 and November 15
  • Mobile home: August 31 and November 15
  • Personal property: May 15

A mailed payment is timely only when its postmark is on or before the due date. If the deadline is close, hand the envelope to the postmaster and ask for a postmark.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Chisago County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late second-half penalties

The county publishes a separate table for each property type. This one covers the second-half payment on residential homestead and cabin property, plus the case where both halves are unpaid.

Penalty on unpaid second-half tax, homestead and cabin property
Not paid beforeSecond half onlyBoth halves unpaid
October 162%5%
November 14%6%
December 15%6.5%
January 27%8.5%

Non-homestead rates run higher: a first-half payment made after October 1 carries 12%, and 14% after January 2.

Penalty stops when a bill turns delinquent on the first business day of January. Interest then starts under Minn. Stat. 270.03 at 8% a year, charged as simple interest each month on the tax, penalty and publication fee.

Delinquent taxes

Any tax left unpaid from a prior year is delinquent. By February 15 the county auditor files the delinquent list with the district court administrator, a step tied to Minn. Stat. 279.05. Minn. Stat. 279.09 then has the list published in the county's official newspaper by March 20, with a second printing at least two weeks later. The county charges $25 per parcel to recover that cost.

  • Only full payment of all delinquent tax removes a parcel from the list.
  • Partial payments cut the balance and the interest, but they do not stop forfeiture.
  • If the balance is not paid by the end of the redemption period, usually three years but it varies by class, the property can be forfeited.
  • Anyone near the end of that period should call the office to ask about options.

Homestead and mobile home sales

An owner who lives in the home as a primary residence, or whose qualifying relative lives there, applies to the county assessor on the Homestead Application. Completed forms are due by December 31, in person or by mail. Other tracks cover relative homestead, service-connected disability, manufactured home, special agricultural, blind or disabled (class 1b) and first-time home buyer. A spouse may claim a separate homestead in cases such as pending dissolution, legal separation or a job that keeps the spouse at least 50 miles away.

Moving or selling a mobile home takes a Tax Release Letter signed by the Auditor-Treasurer showing no tax owed. The seller must show a current title in the seller's name first, and the buyer takes both the title and the letter to a Minnesota motor vehicle office. The nearest is the Chisago City DMV.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chisago County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your valuation

In March the assessor mails a Valuation and Classification Notice that lists market value, class, new improvements and exclusions such as homestead. Call the assessor first. Most Chisago County communities then hold a Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, and an owner who still disagrees may go to the County Board of Appeal and Equalization. You can appeal value and classification, but not the tax itself.

Every parcel is valued as of January 2, and appraisers visit each property about once every five years. For the January 2, 2026 assessment, the assessor used sales from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025, and each sale's Certificate of Real Estate Value helps separate open-market sales from bank-owned or family transfers. Under Minn. Stat. 274.01, an owner who was told of a proposed increase and neither appeared nor wrote to the local board cannot go on to the county board. For budget complaints, use the Truth in Taxation meetings or the annual township meeting.

Before you list

Pull the current statement and confirm that both halves are paid or scheduled. The county site has an online property search for recent and prior years, an interactive GIS map, a property tax calculator and an address change form for statements. After you sell, update your mailing address. The owner of record is the one who receives the next statement.

Check the class on your statement too. A homestead classification lowers tax, and the buyer will have to apply for it separately. Parcels with forfeited or delinquent history should be cleared first, because only full payment takes a parcel off the delinquent list. When in doubt, call 651-213-8500 and ask for the amount owed through a specific date.

In a cash sale the title company still pays any open balance from your proceeds, so the payoff figure is the same.

Local market context

Chisago County runs 415 square miles of land along the St. Croix River and the Wisconsin border. Population is 59,142. Cities include Center City, Chisago City, Lindstrom, North Branch (the largest), Rush City, Shafer, Taylors Falls and Wyoming.

  • Median owner-occupied home value: $351,900
  • Owner-occupied rate: 85.9%
  • Median household income: $99,400
  • Building permits, 2025: 240

Every city has its own council, and the county posts the meeting schedules.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When are Chisago County property taxes due?

Real estate taxes are due May 15 and October 15. Agricultural property pays the second half on November 15, and mobile homes pay on August 31 and November 15.

What if my Chisago County tax statement never came?

You still owe the tax. Statements are generated in mid-February for the owner of record then, so a buyer after that date gets none. Print one from the county website or call 651-213-8500.

What interest does Chisago County charge on delinquent tax?

Interest starts on the first business day of January and runs at 8% a year, as simple interest charged monthly. It applies to the tax, penalty and publication fee.

How long before Chisago County can forfeit my property?

Unpaid tax goes through a redemption period that varies by class and usually lasts three years. Only full payment stops forfeiture, so call the office before the period ends.

How do I apply for homestead in Chisago County?

File the Homestead Application with the county assessor, in person or by mail, by December 31. The owner must live in the home as a primary residence, or a qualifying relative must.

Otter Tail County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota

  • Otter Tail County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Otter Tail County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Otter Tail County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Otter Tail County?

Assessor, Treasurer, Auditor and Recorder

The county's government offices are at the Government Services Center, 500 West Fir Avenue, Fergus Falls, MN 56537. The Assessor handles value and class at 218-998-8010. The Treasurer takes payments and questions at 218-998-8295, the Auditor can be reached at 218-998-8030, and the Recorder, who files deeds, is at 218-998-8140.

Appraisers working out of the Assessor's office review about 65,000 parcels across 62 townships and 22 cities. They run annual sales studies, and the Minnesota Department of Revenue requires the county's estimated values to land between 90% and 105% of actual market value. Every owner is mailed a spring notice that lists the new value, the class and the appeal dates.

With that many parcels, classification carries weight. The department sorts property by primary use, such as residential, agricultural, seasonal or commercial, and a lake cabin is taxed differently from a year-round house.

Housing in Otter Tail County

Fergus Falls is the seat and biggest city, and lakes are everywhere in the county, so plenty of parcels are cabins and seasonal homes. Population is 61,041, with 27.6% aged 65 or older. There are 37,036 housing units but only 25,157 households, and 79.5% of occupied units are owner-occupied. Median owner-occupied value is $273,000 and median gross rent is $868.

The gap between housing units and households shows how many parcels are not a primary residence. Whether a parcel counts as homestead or seasonal changes the rate and the penalty schedule, so check the class on your notice before you set a price.

Tax calendar

The county posts one calendar covering assessment, appeals and payment, and a Saturday or Sunday due date slides forward to the first business day after it. These are the entries that matter most to an owner.

Selected Otter Tail County property tax dates
DateEvent
January 2Assessment date for real and personal property
April 30Deadline for a Tax Court petition on value
May 15First half of real property tax; also first half of agricultural tax
May 31First half for resort and certain seasonal commercial property
August 15Deadline to file a Property Tax Refund Return
October 15Second half of real estate tax, unless part is agricultural
November 15Second half for classes 1b, 2a and 2b agricultural property and manufactured homes
December 31Final date to establish homestead for the current year

No second-half statement is mailed to you, and the Treasurer turns away checks dated in the future. Late charges for every class come from section 279.01, which charges 2% on homestead and 4% on nonhomestead property for a missed date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Otter Tail County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Paying the Treasurer

You can pay in any of these ways:

  • Online by e-check at $1.00 per transaction, or by card at 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum; enter the parcel number without the leading R, P or M
  • Automatic withdrawal, using the county's Automatic Withdrawal Form returned to the Treasurer
  • Mail, with checks payable to Otter Tail County and a U.S. Postal Service postmark as proof of timely mailing
  • In person at the Treasurer's counter, or in the drop box at the entrance during business hours, with another drop box in the parking lot for after-hours payments

If you pay through your bank's bill pay, set it up early so the check is dated before the deadline. A private postage meter mark does not count, so ask the post office to hand-cancel the envelope when in doubt.

How a value appeal works

The valuation notice shows up in March and April. Read both sides, then phone the Assessor with any questions about the number. If the call does not resolve it, the steps are:

  1. Present the case to your Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, made up of the township board or city council. These boards convene April 1 to 20.
  2. Where the area holds an Open Book meeting instead, contact your appraiser from the Contact My Assessor list.
  3. Take it to the countywide board, which convenes in June on up to ten meeting days after the second Friday.
  4. File with the Minnesota Tax Court. It is open even to owners who skipped the earlier steps, and the deadline is April 30 of the taxes-payable year.

Owners may also serve a petition on the county auditor under 278.01. Resort owners watch an earlier date: January 15 is the last day to submit for class 1c or 4c(5) resort classification.

If taxes go unpaid before a sale

Three years after the judgment year, tax that is still unpaid sends the parcel to the State of Minnesota, and the Auditor-Treasurer later offers it to the highest bidder at a public sale. Anyone owing delinquent real or personal property tax in the county is barred from bidding. Staff cannot arrange viewings of forfeited property before a sale. If a parcel sells for more than the minimum bid, interested parties have six months from the first notice of surplus to claim the extra money (Minnesota Statutes 282.005).

In a normal sale, the county auditor looks at the parcel under section 272.12 and says whether any delinquent tax is owed, and only then can the deed be recorded. Ask the Auditor at 218-998-8030 for the payoff figure well before the closing date, and the Recorder at 218-998-8140 about filing.

A sensible order of work: get the payoff figure, confirm your class with the Assessor, and pass both to the title company. Cash buyers avoid a lender's underwriting, yet the auditor must still clear the tax before the deed goes on record.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Otter Tail County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Prepping a sale of a lake or rural parcel

Sellers of cabins and rural parcels have more to sort out than town homeowners. Start by reading the class printed on your valuation notice. A seasonal or resort class means a different rate and a different first-half date than a homestead, and the buyer's lender will want to know which one applies.

Then ask the Treasurer which halves are paid, and whether an agricultural portion follows the later November date. The Recorder can tell you what your side must supply to file the deed. Gather the parcel number, the last statement and any special assessment notice before you meet a buyer or a title company. If you are selling for cash, the same office checks apply, but you can skip the waiting that comes with a lender's payoff letter and escrow reconciliation.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Otter Tail County Treasurer's phone number?

Dial 218-998-8295 for the Treasurer, whose office is at 500 West Fir Avenue in Fergus Falls. The Assessor, who answers value and classification questions, is at 218-998-8010.

When is the Otter Tail County second-half tax due?

Most real estate is due October 15. Classes 1b, 2a and 2b agricultural property and manufactured homes are due November 15. Weekend dates slide to Monday, and no second-half statement is mailed.

What are the Otter Tail online payment fees?

E-checks run $1.00 each. Cards cost 2.5%, with a $2.00 minimum. Leave off the R, P or M at the start of the parcel number. No fee applies to checks or counter payments.

Who handles Otter Tail County resort and seasonal property classification?

That is the Assessor's Office. Owners seeking class 1c or 4c(5) resort classification must apply by January 15, and May 31 is the first-half date for seasonal commercial property. Call 218-998-8010 with questions.

Can I still appeal to the Tax Court if I skipped the local board?

Yes. The Tax Court accepts petitions from owners who never went to a board. File by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

Who collects and assesses

The Cass County Auditor-Treasurer collects the tax at the courthouse, 303 Minnesota Avenue W, second floor, in Walker. Phone (218) 547-7260 and mail to PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm. Besides property tax, the department runs elections, vital statistics, licensing and the parcel mapping system.

Value and classification belong to the county assessor at (218) 547-7298. Valuation runs through a single county-wide system, so one office values every township parcel and no local assessors are involved. Staff appraisers view each property about once every five years and look at all new construction and alterations in the current year.

Due dates

The first half of real property tax is due May 15, and the non-farm second half is due October 15. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay their second half on November 15. A deadline that falls on a weekend or legal holiday slides to the next business day, and personal property taxes share the real property schedule.

Cass County tax due dates by property type
Due dateProperty and installment
May 15Real property, first half (or the whole bill if it is $100 or less)
May 31Resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half (or all if $50 or less)
October 15Non-farm real property, second half
November 15Farm real property and manufactured homes, second half

The May 31 resort date comes from Minn. Stat. 279.01. It extends the date to commercial seasonal recreational property in classes 1c and 4c and to class 3a property that earns over 60 percent of its gross income in May through August. A class 3a owner attaches an affidavit, and the county asks eligible businesses to return its Commercial Tax Deferral Form.

Ways to pay

The county's payment page lists these routes:

  • At the courthouse during office hours.
  • By mail to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer with the right stub, postmarked before the due date. The second-half stub sits directly above the first-half stub at the bottom of the statement.
  • Autopay through MuniciPay. An ACH payment costs $1.00 and a card costs 2.25% of the payment with a $1.00 minimum.
  • By phone at (218) 321-9802, with a confirmation number noted down.
  • Through a mortgage escrow account. If a lender pays the bill, your statement copy says that taxes paid by an escrow agent should not be paid again.

Electronic payments take about two business days to post, so do not wait for the due date. Near a deadline, ask the local postmaster to hand-stamp a mailed envelope. Fees on electronic payments go to the service provider, not the county.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cass County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Refuse management fee

Improved parcels here carry a flat refuse management fee when assessed value is at least $1,000. The charge began in 1990, was once called the solid waste fee, and funds waste disposal and recycling programs. The county board has kept it as a flat fee instead of folding the cost into the levy.

  • Residential and seasonal properties: $86
  • Commercial under $9,999 in building value: $86
  • Commercial from $10,000 to $99,999: $195
  • Commercial from $100,000 to $499,999: $391
  • Commercial at $500,000 and up: $652
  • Apartments: $16 per unit
  • Non-commercial tax-exempt buildings: $86

Any improved parcel you sell will carry this line, so the buyer's first bill includes it.

Questioning your value or homestead

The notice of assessed value mailed each spring explains how to appeal. The assessor's office answers questions all year at (218) 547-7298. Local boards of appeal sit between April 1 and May 31 under Minn. Stat. 274.01, and anyone who is told of a proposed increase and fails to show up or write in may not go on to the county board.

Market value is set as of January 2 each year. The state expects an assessor's value to land between 90% and 105% of sale price. File a homestead application with the assessor. The same office can tell blind or disabled owners whether they qualify for the relief Minnesota offers them. The state runs the refund program for homeowners, so use the Department of Revenue forms and instructions for those questions.

Selling and the tax record

Give the Auditor-Treasurer your new mailing address the day you move. A wrong address can delay or block time-sensitive statements and other property mailings, and care-of addresses can be added. No owner name is changed in the tax records without a recorded legal document.

A short checklist before you list: find your most recent statement and both stubs, confirm the class printed on it, ask the assessor to confirm your homestead status, and note the refuse fee amount. Having these ready also makes it easy for a buyer, a lender or a cash buyer's title company to verify the parcel and set the closing figures.

If you are working through a contract for deed, read the county's Property Tax Billing and Collection Procedures fact sheet, which explains who receives the statement.

Before closing, ask the Auditor-Treasurer for the balance on the parcel, including the refuse fee line. A cash sale skips the lender, so the title company will settle the tax from your proceeds at the table.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cass County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid taxes and forfeiture

Interest begins on unpaid balances after January 2 of the following year, and penalties and rates follow state statute. Partial payments are accepted on prior-year taxes, with a $100 minimum preferred. The money goes to the newest year first and then back through earlier years. Nonpayment can end in loss of the property through forfeiture under Minnesota law.

Call the Auditor-Treasurer at (218) 547-7260 for the amount past due on a parcel, and ask for the figure as of your expected closing date. If you sell on a contract for deed, only the new contract holder receives the bill, but you still have to watch that the taxes get paid.

Local market context

Cass County is large and quiet. It has 2,022 square miles of land, a population of 31,430, and 25,344 housing units against 12,874 households, which points to a large stock of seasonal and second homes. Walker holds the courthouse, and Lake Shore is the biggest city. Median owner-occupied home value is $288,300.

Class 4c seasonal recreational property takes the homestead penalty schedule. If you are listing a lake cabin in a township such as Pine River, Shingobee or Boy Lake, check the class on the statement and the payment dates that go with it.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Cass County payment deadlines?

May 15 for the first half of real property and October 15 for the second half of non-farm property. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay the second half on November 15, and resorts have until May 31.

Can I pay Cass County property tax online?

Yes, through MuniciPay. ACH costs $1.00 per payment and a debit or credit card costs 2.25% with a $1.00 minimum. Allow two business days for posting.

Where do I send a Cass County tax payment?

Send it to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer, PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484, with the stub from your statement, or bring it to the courthouse at 303 Minnesota Avenue W.

What is the $86 charge on a Cass County tax statement?

It is the refuse management fee that applies to residential and seasonal parcels with an assessed value of at least $1,000. It pays for waste disposal and recycling in the county.

Who decides my Cass County homestead status?

The Cass County Assessor's Office reviews homestead applications. Call (218) 547-7298 to apply or to check the status.

Crow Wing County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Crow Wing County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Crow Wing County, MN Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Crow Wing County, MN Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Crow Wing County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Crow Wing County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Crow Wing County?
We buy Crow Wing County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Who handles property tax

Land Services, a single department, assesses property and collects the tax in Crow Wing County. It is at 322 Laurel Street in Brainerd, the county seat, and answers at 218-824-1010.

The staff there mail bills, take payments, field valuation questions and maintain the field books and parcel records that anyone can research on the lower level. The county's Property Search website shows parcel data, and you can pull a duplicate tax statement by parcel ID or address.

Selling a lake-country house

Crow Wing is lake country in east central Minnesota, with roughly 417 named lakes, the Mississippi running through, and wooded rolling ground across 999 square miles of land. About 69,132 people live here, up 4.6% from the 2020 base.

The county counts 44,306 housing units and 29,402 households. In 2020 about 32.9% of units were vacant, which points to a big stock of cabins. Owners live in 77.0% of occupied homes, and the typical value is $306,800. Builders took out 625 permits in 2025. Brainerd, Baxter, Crosby, Crosslake, Garrison, Nisswa, Pequot Lakes, Breezy Point, Deerwood and Fort Ripley are among the communities.

With so much lakeshore, classification does a lot of work. A homestead and a seasonal cabin are taxed under different rules, so confirm which one your parcel carries before you price it.

Payment dates

A real estate bill is paid in halves, the first due May 15 and the second due October 15. Farmland has until November 15 for its second half. Mobile homes are billed on August 31 and November 15.

A resort or business that earns more than 60% of its gross income between May and August can file an affidavit moving the first-half date to May 31, and the affidavit has to go in with the payment. Any real estate half left unpaid is already carrying penalty.

Tax still open on December 31 of its due year turns delinquent. For delinquent years, the county wants a call to Land Services at 218-824-1010 before you pay, so the amount is right. Under Minnesota Statutes section 280.39, payments are applied to the newest years first.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Crow Wing County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late penalty schedule

A state-set table drives the penalty, and the county posts it. An unpaid first half climbs the fastest, as the county's figures show.

Penalty on an unpaid first half
DateHomestead and cabinsNon-homestead
May 162%4%
June 14%8%
July 15%9%
August 16%10%
September 17%11%
October 18%12%

Manufactured homes pay 8% from September 1 on the first half, and personal property pays 8% from May 16. The treasurer may also abate a penalty once when a check was mailed with a postmark within a business day of the deadline.

Ways to pay

Land Services takes payment four ways.

  • Online: an e-check costs $1.95, and a card costs 2.35% of the payment or $1.95, whichever is greater, up to $50,000. The processor keeps those fees, not the county. Credit takes three to four days to post.
  • For online payment you need the 8-digit parcel number, and you choose Pay Full Year to settle both halves.
  • At the counter, weekdays from eight to 4:30, with an outdoor drop box that is always open.
  • By mail: send the remittance stub and payment to Land Services, 322 Laurel Street Ste 15, Brainerd, MN 56401.

How values are set and how to push back

Every parcel is revalued each year, and the county must land between 90% and 105% of market value. Staff walk each property once every five years and check building permits. Comparable sales drive the number, adjusted for land, size, quality and condition, and the class follows current use.

Two routes exist for a disagreement. The first runs through the boards: a local board or open book meeting, then the county board, which you must phone ahead to be placed on. Where a city or township has no local board, owners go to an open book session before the county board. The second route is the Minnesota Tax Court.

  • Meeting times and places are printed on your Notice of Valuation and Classification.
  • You can appear in person, send a letter, or authorize a representative.
  • A court petition is due April 30 of the year the bill is payable (section 278.01).
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Crow Wing County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief programs

The county's Taxes page points to Minnesota Department of Revenue guidance for owners who might pay less. Many need a filing before a deadline, so ask Land Services which fit your parcel.

  • Homestead classification and the homestead market value exclusion for owner-occupied houses.
  • Special homestead classification for blind or disabled owners.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral.
  • A market value exclusion for owners with a service-connected disability.
  • 2c managed forest land and the Sustainable Forest Incentive Act.
  • Green Acres and rural preserve deferral for agricultural and rural vacant land, plus special agricultural homestead.
  • Property tax refunds.

An owner who is behind can pay part of a bill. The treasurer may take less than the full installment, and section 279.01 sends the money to the oldest unpaid installment first. A short payment goes to accrued penalty before tax. Partial payment does not satisfy the minimum needed to keep an appeal alive.

Unpaid tax at a sale

Delinquent tax stops recording: the auditor must clear the land first (section 272.12). A sale over $3,000 also brings a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115), and the seller's homestead class falls away until the buyer applies and qualifies.

Request a payoff for each parcel from Land Services, since lake property sales often include several. A buyer may also care about the relief programs the assessing office lists, such as 2c managed forest, the disability exclusion, Green Acres, homesteading and rural preserve.

For a clean closing, gather the parcel IDs, check the Property Search site for open balances, and bring the figures to your title company early so the payoff comes out of proceeds.

Before you list a Crow Wing property

Start at Land Services with three questions. What class does each parcel carry, homestead or seasonal? Is any half of this year's bill still open, or any older year? When was the property last walked by an appraiser? The answers shape your asking price and the payoff the title company will request.

If you rent the place out part of the year, the class may differ from what you assume. A lake cabin used by family only, with no one living there year-round, is not a homestead, and a buyer who plans to live there must file for the class on their own.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Crow Wing County property taxes?

Pay Land Services at 322 Laurel Street Ste 15 in Brainerd, online, by mail or in the drop box. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-824-1010.

What are the Crow Wing County due dates?

Real estate is due May 15 and October 15, the agricultural second half on November 15, and mobile homes on August 31 and November 15. Each new year brings the same schedule.

How much is the late penalty on a Crow Wing County homestead?

It begins at 2% on an unpaid first half after May 15 and reaches 8% by October 1. Non-homestead property starts at 4% and tops out at 12%.

Can I challenge my Crow Wing County valuation?

Yes, through the local and county boards each spring and June, or by Tax Court petition due April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Call Land Services at 218-824-1010 and ask for the assessor.

Do delinquent Crow Wing County taxes need to be paid before a sale?

Yes, the deed cannot be recorded until they are cleared. Call Land Services at 218-824-1010 before paying so staff can confirm the right amount and avoid extra penalty.

Isanti County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Isanti County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Isanti County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Isanti County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Isanti County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Isanti County?
We buy Isanti County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Which offices bill and value your house?

Value and billing are handled by different people. The Assessor puts a market value and a class on every parcel, working from Minnesota statutes and Department of Revenue standards. The Auditor-Treasurer turns that into a bill and collects it. Write to the Assessor at 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, MN 55008. Cambridge doubles as the county seat.

The Assessor's office also hands out the forms for agricultural use, homestead, local option disaster abatement and managed forest. If you have a question about a bill, a classification or a payoff, these are the two counters to start with.

Isanti County housing snapshot

Isanti County is a fast-growing exurb in east-central Minnesota that belongs to the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metro area. Anoka County lies to its south. The cities are Cambridge, Isanti, Braham (partly in Kanabec County) and St. Francis (mostly in Anoka County). The population reached 44,386 by mid-2025, up 7.9% from 41,128 in April 2020.

Housing units total 18,068, and builders pulled 276 permits in 2025. Owners live in about 83.7% of homes, which means most sellers are longtime holders. The median owner-occupied home is worth $306,200. Rural parcels can sit in agricultural, managed forest or Green Acres programs, each with its own application date. The median says little about your own bill, so get the real numbers from the Auditor-Treasurer.

Due dates by property type

Most residential and agricultural owners pay the first half by May 15 and the second by October 15. Agricultural second halves move to November 15, and manufactured homes keep a separate calendar. All personal property tax is due in full by May 15.

Isanti County due dates by property type
Due dateWhat is due
May 15First half, residential and agricultural
August 31First half, manufactured homes (whole bill if $50 or less)
October 15Second half, residential only
November 15Second half, manufactured homes and agricultural

A mailed payment is on time when the postmark is dated no later than the due date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Isanti County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a late payment costs

Pay after the deadline and Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 starts a penalty clock: 2% if the home is a homestead, 4% if it is not.

Come the first of the next month with the half still unpaid, and that percentage is charged again. Every later month through December tacks on 1% more. The most you can owe in penalty is 8% on a homestead and 12% on anything else. A rental house or vacant inherited home usually falls in the higher group, so an estate that leaves an Isanti County house unpaid for a few months can end up with a double-digit penalty.

There is one forgiveness rule: if your payment is mailed and postmarked no more than a business day after the due date, the treasurer must waive the penalty, once, for an owner who has not used it before.

How to appeal an Isanti County valuation

The order is assessor, then your city or township board of appeal and equalization, then the county board, with court as the final step.

Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 opens two court doors. A district court petition must be served on the county auditor and filed with the court administrator by April 30 of the year the bill is payable. A Tax Court appeal can begin once the valuation notice arrives and must begin before May 1 of that year. Local board meeting dates are posted on the county calendar after notices go out, so check back in spring.

Appealing does not excuse payment. Section 279.01 lets the treasurer take partial payments, and doing so does not waive the minimum payment needed to keep an appeal alive under section 278.03. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer what that minimum is before you file.

Application deadlines for homeowners

The assessor's application calendar follows the assessment year, and a late filing usually takes effect a year later. These are the cutoffs:

  • Homestead, plus actively farming or special agricultural homestead: December 31.
  • Blind or disabled special homestead: October 1.
  • Mobile home homesteads: May 31.
  • Green Acres, Rural Preserve, managed forest land and nonprofit community service organizations: May 1.
  • Exempt properties: July 1. Sustainable forest: September 30.

Agricultural use has to be in place by January 2 of the assessment year to count for the following payable year. Separately, the state's Homestead Credit Refund is due August 15, and a claim is still accepted for a year past that date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Isanti County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a rural or farm parcel

Land outside the cities often carries a special classification, and that is worth sorting out before a buyer asks. Green Acres, Rural Preserve and managed forest land all need an application on file by May 1. Agricultural use must already be in place on January 2 of the assessment year to count for the next payable year. A buyer who wants to keep a program running should talk to the Assessor early, because the application dates above do not move to fit a closing.

Ask the assessor for the current class of every parcel you are selling, and pull the matching forms from the same office. If a piece of the land is farmed and another piece is a house site, each may be classed differently, and a late filing on either one usually pushes the benefit out by a full year.

What to bring to the county office

A short visit goes faster with the right papers. Bring your parcel number, your most recent tax statement and the date you hope to close. Ask for a printed payoff that includes penalty and any special assessment, and ask which of the programs on your parcel, such as homestead or agricultural use, end when the deed changes hands.

Taxes when you sell an Isanti County house

Tax stays attached to the land, not the owner, which means anything unpaid is cleared on or before closing day. Give the Auditor-Treasurer your parcel number and ask for the total owed, penalty and special assessments included.

With an escrow account, the lender sends the money and your statement tells you not to pay. Your purchase contract spells out who covers which part of the current year. Take your latest statement and closing date with you to the treasurer's office, so the figure they give you lines up with the payoff the title company requests.

A workable sequence: find your statement and parcel number, request the amount owed through the day you expect to close, and confirm the home still counts as a homestead, because a change in how it is used affects both classification and penalty rate. An inherited or long-empty house deserves a question about earlier years too. A payoff quote that skips them will not clear the title.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the second half deadline for a regular Isanti County home?

October 15 for a residential property. Agricultural and manufactured home second halves run to November 15, and a mailed payment counts if it is postmarked by the due date.

Where is the Isanti County Assessor located?

The Assessor takes applications by mail at 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, MN 55008. Cambridge is also the county seat.

Can I appeal my Isanti County value after the spring meetings?

Yes, in court. A district court petition is due April 30 of the payable year, and a Tax Court appeal can start after the valuation notice arrives and before May 1, under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01.

How much is the late penalty on an Isanti County rental house?

It starts at 4% on a nonhomestead parcel and can reach 12% by December, under section 279.01. A homestead starts at 2% and tops out at 8%.

When should I file for homestead in Isanti County?

By December 31 of the assessment year, so it applies to taxes payable the next year. The blind or disabled special homestead cutoff is October 1.

Goodhue County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Goodhue County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Goodhue County, MN Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Goodhue County, MN Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Goodhue County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Goodhue County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Goodhue County?
We buy Goodhue County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Goodhue County housing for sellers

Across Lake Pepin from Wisconsin, Goodhue County holds southeastern Minnesota's river bluffs, and Red Wing is its seat. The ground is rolling hills and bluffs cut by the Cannon River, and traffic runs on U.S. 52, 61 and 63. Cities include Red Wing, Cannon Falls, Zumbrota, Kenyon, Wanamingo, Goodhue and pieces of Lake City and Pine Island.

  • About 48,195 residents, up 1.3% since the 2020 census.
  • 19,727 households, with 78.8% of homes lived in by their owners.
  • A median owner-occupied home value of $285,100 and a median household income of $84,171.
  • 84 building permits in 2025 across 21,445 housing units.

Several school districts levy on county homes, so the same price can mean a different bill from one address to the next.

Which office handles property tax

Finance and Taxpayer Services runs both the assessor and the auditor/treasurer from the second floor of the Government Center, 509 W. 5th St. in Red Wing. The phone is 651-385-3040 and the counter is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For assessor questions, choose option 1.

The county's board controls only the county budget and levy. A bill can move for thirteen reasons, among them a change in your value, a shift in other owners' values, city or township levies, school levies, referendums, special assessments and state aid or law changes. Only the county piece belongs to the commissioners. A seller who sees a jump should find out which piece moved before calling.

Due dates and penalties

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 splits the bill into two halves, payable before May 16 and before October 16 when the tax on a parcel is over $100. Agricultural homestead and qualifying farm land can pay the second half without penalty through November 15.

A late homestead bill is charged 2 percent and a late nonhomestead bill 4 percent starting the day after the due date. The charge is applied again on the first of the next month, after which 1 percent is added monthly through December. The ceilings are 8 percent and 12 percent. The treasurer must abate a late penalty once if the envelope was postmarked within one business day of the due date and the owner has not used that abatement before.

The Finance page has a link labeled Search Property Tax Records/Pay Property Tax for lookups and payments, and staff will quote a parcel payoff ahead of closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Goodhue County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How the county arrives at your value

As of January 2, the assessor estimates value and class for over 29,000 parcels, and the figure sets taxes payable the following year. Staff try to view the inside and outside of each home, listing size, age, quality, basement finish and extras. That feeds a mass appraisal system a county appraiser reviews. The sales window that guides the estimate runs October 1 through September 30 before the assessment date.

State rules require a physical review of every property at least once every five years, and an overall level of assessment between 90 and 105 percent of market value. The county says it consistently meets that test. Class matters as much as value: homestead, nonhomestead residential, apartment and commercial are each taxed at a percentage the legislature sets. On-site reassessments take place in several areas each cycle, so if your neighborhood is on the list, expect a request to visit.

Rules that vary within the county

Ten cities, whole or partial, and 21 townships make up the county, and every one sets its own levy on top of the county and school district levies. A house in Red Wing and a farmhouse in Vasa Township share a county assessor but face different local boards, different school districts and sometimes different reassessment schedules.

If a letter asks for an interior viewing, answer it. That gives the appraiser accurate facts about finish, condition and extras, which is easier than arguing about them after the notice arrives. Owners who think the value and classification on their notice are right do not need to contact the assessor at all.

Appealing an assessment

Lead with evidence. Collect recent comparable sales and any market analysis, then phone the assessor at 651-385-3040 option 1 and walk an appraiser through them. An interior inspection can be scheduled. If the question is still open, go to the local board of appeal and equalization, then make an appointment with the county board, which meets in June by appointment only. The call to book it goes through the same number.

Goodhue County appeal path
StepWhereWhat to do
1AssessorGather sales, call 651-385-3040 option 1, review with an appraiser
2Interior inspectionSchedule if the appraiser asks
3Local boardAttend the meeting for your city or township
4County boardAppointment only, 509 W. 5th St., Red Wing
5Minnesota Tax CourtPhone 651-539-3260; filing deadline April 30

Only the current year valuation can go through the boards. An appeal of a prior year value runs through Tax Court alone, and Statutes 278.01 sets April 30 of the tax year as the court filing date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Goodhue County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Checklist before listing

  • The valuation notice mailed in March, for the estimated market value and the class assigned to the home.
  • Whether the home is still classified as homestead for the owner who is selling.
  • Whether the neighborhood is in a reassessment group this cycle.
  • Both halves of the current year tax, and any older balance on the parcel.
  • Whether any appeal is pending, since Tax Court filings for a tax year close on April 30.

Finance and Taxpayer Services can answer the tax and assessor items at 651-385-3040. Once a buyer signs, the title company takes over the payoff.

What happens to the tax bill at a sale

Delinquent tax comes first. Before a transfer, Minnesota Statutes 272.12 has the auditor review the deed for delinquent tax. The recorder files nothing lacking the auditor's note. If the sale covers only part of a parcel, Statutes 272.121 calls for the treasurer's certification that the full-parcel tax for the current year is paid.

For an ordinary whole-parcel sale, ask the title company how this year's first and second halves will be split, and ask Finance and Taxpayer Services for the amount still open on the parcel. Buyers who plan to live in the home should apply for homestead. People who bought or moved into a property in the past year may also qualify for a property tax refund.

A cash buyer still goes through the same deed check, so the payoff step does not disappear. It just happens without a lender in the middle.

Frequently asked questions

Who sets property values in Goodhue County?

The county assessor, working from the Government Center in Red Wing. Values are set as of January 2 and mailed to owners in March. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 with questions.

When does the Goodhue County board of appeal and equalization meet?

In June, by appointment only. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 to book a time, after trying the local board for your city or township.

Can I appeal last year's Goodhue County value?

Only through Minnesota Tax Court. Prior year values cannot go to the county boards, and the court filing must be made by April 30 of the year the taxes are due.

What are the Goodhue County tax due dates?

Half is due before May 16 and half before October 16, under Minnesota Statutes 279.01. Qualifying agricultural property can pay the second half by November 15 without penalty.

Do I need to pay delinquent tax to sell my Goodhue County home?

Yes. A deed cannot be recorded until the auditor certifies no delinquent tax remains, so the payoff is normally handled at closing by the title company.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in McLeod County?

Get My Cash Offer →

Check these before you list

Two offices decide what a parcel owes. The assessor picks the value and the class, and the Auditor-Treasurer in Glencoe turns those into a bill and collects it. Before listing, confirm three things: the current half is paid, no special assessment is attached, and you know what happens to the homestead class at closing. Each can change what you net, and one phone call settles each.

  • Auditor-Treasurer, 520 Chandler Avenue North, Glencoe: 320-864-1203 for payments and 320-864-1271 for tax balance questions.
  • County Assessor: 320-864-1254 for valuation, class and homestead forms.

McLeod County housing in brief

McLeod County lies west of the Twin Cities in south central Minnesota. Glencoe holds the courthouse, while Hutchinson has the most people. Other cities are Biscay, Brownton, Lester Prairie, Plato, Silver Lake, Stewart and Winsted.

The county counted 36,771 people in 2020 and estimates 36,631 for July 2025. Of its 16,162 housing units, 77.4% of occupied ones are owner occupied. A typical owned home was valued at $246,100 for 2020 to 2024, and 206 building permits were issued in 2025. About 55.5% of residents lived in urban areas in 2020 and 44.5% in rural ones, so a seller might hold a Hutchinson lot, a farmstead near Brownton or a lake cabin, and each is taxed in its own class.

Due dates

Ordinary real estate and personal property are due May 15 and October 15. Farmland has a later calendar and manufactured homes keep their own.

McLeod County annual property tax due dates
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estate and personal propertyMay 15October 15
Agricultural propertyMay 15November 15
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

Statements are mailed in March, and state law sets March 31 as the deadline. Manufactured home statements are planned for June, with a July 15 deadline. Not receiving yours does not cancel the tax, so ask the Auditor-Treasurer for a duplicate. If you are mid-sale, get that copy early. The buyer's lender and the title company both ask for the parcel number and the amount.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McLeod County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to pay

Six payment routes are open to you. Pick one that fits around your closing date.

  • Walk in with a check or cash to the Government Center in Glencoe.
  • Mail a check payable to McLeod County Auditor-Treasurer. The postmark must fall on or before the due date, and since servicing centers may stamp it two or three days after you drop it off, mail early.
  • Use a credit card or eCheck online or by phone. Cards cost 2.5% of the transaction, and an eCheck costs $1.50 below $10,000 and $10.00 at or above it.
  • Use the secure drop box out front of the Government Center. Whatever is inside at 8:00 a.m. is treated as the previous day's business.
  • Sign up for direct debit from a bank account at least a month ahead of the due date.
  • Let your lender pay from mortgage escrow.

In the online search, type just the numeric part of the parcel ID and pick the roll type from the drop-down.

Late payments

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 charges 2% on a late homestead half and 4% on any other late half. That repeats on the first day of the following month, and 1% per month follows through December. Penalty never exceeds 8% on a homestead or 12% on other property. The state sample tax statement shows the current table.

Taxes turn delinquent in the calendar year after they are due, and from then on interest and penalty accrue monthly as the parcel moves toward judgment and forfeiture. The office will accept more or less than the exact installment, and a partial payment goes to that year's penalty first. You can get the penalty abated once if your mailed payment is postmarked within a business day of the due date and you have never used that relief.

How to appeal your value

The assessor's office sets market value and class, and the Auditor-Treasurer applies the local rate to it. A deputy assessor and four appraisers divide the county by area. The deputy assessor handles Hutchinson plus every apartment and commercial parcel, an appraiser covers Glencoe, Lester Prairie and Winsted, and the county's staff page lists who covers each township and smaller city. The Department of Revenue requires every property to be viewed, and a visit takes about 15 minutes or less. An owner can decline the inspection, and the appraiser then judges value from outside.

A challenge climbs three steps under Minnesota Statutes chapters 274 and 278:

  • Local board of appeal and equalization: your town board or city council sits sometime from April 1 to May 31 and wraps up within 20 days. Its combined reductions cannot cut the assessor's total by more than one percent.
  • County board: the commissioners and the auditor take what the local board left open. Owners who ignored a notice at the local level may be barred from this stage.
  • Tax Court or district court: the petition and proof of service must be filed by the end of April in the payable year.

Before filing anything, phone the assessor and share a few comparable sales. It costs nothing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy McLeod County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and refunds

Homestead is the largest saving for most owners, and living in the property by December 1 qualifies you to apply for the next year. A closing resets it: under 272.115 the assessor drops the homestead class after a transfer unless the buyer applies and qualifies. If the buyer forgets, the next year's bill will be higher, so bring it up while you negotiate.

The county's FAQ also covers state refunds. Someone who lived in the property as a homestead on January 2 may get a refund scaled to household income and tax paid, and a second, special refund exists where the bill jumped by more than 12 percent in a year. Form M-1PR claims both, and the Department of Revenue answers form questions at 651-296-4444.

How taxes work when you sell

A deed cannot be recorded in Minnesota without a clean tax record. Section 272.12 makes the auditor search for delinquent taxes before changing the ownership books, and a recorder who ignores that step is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. If the deed covers just a piece of a parcel, the treasurer must certify that this year's tax on the whole parcel is paid (272.121). A sale over $3,000 requires a certificate of value (272.115).

Ask the closing agent how this year's tax gets divided, and ask your lender what will happen to any escrow balance. Street and similar improvement assessments show up on their own line of the statement and stay with the parcel that benefits, so find out from the Auditor-Treasurer what is still unpaid before agreeing on a price.

The November Truth in Taxation notice previews next year's tax. It omits special assessments, and a passed referendum can raise the final number.

Frequently asked questions

Which McLeod County office answers tax questions?

Bills and payments: the Auditor-Treasurer, 320-864-1203 or 320-864-1271. Value, class and homestead: the Assessor, 320-864-1254. Both work from the Government Center, 520 Chandler Avenue North, Glencoe.

What are the McLeod County property tax due dates?

Regular real estate is due May 15 and October 15. Agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15, and manufactured homes are due August 31 and November 15. Statements are mailed in March.

Can I pay McLeod County taxes by credit card?

Yes, on the website or by phone, with a 2.5% vendor charge. An eCheck is $1.50 under $10,000 and $10.00 above. You can also pay with cash, check, the drop box, direct debit or escrow.

Does a McLeod County sale cancel the homestead classification?

For the next assessment year, yes, unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. State law has the assessor remove the class after a transfer, and the owner is expected to report the sale within 30 days.

When must a McLeod County value dispute reach court?

File by April 30 of the payable year. Use the local board in April or May and the county board first, since bypassing them after a notice can cost you the right to appear.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Meeker County?

Who to call in Meeker County

Three offices in Litchfield share the work. The Auditor builds each bill, the Treasurer collects it, and the Assessor supplies the value and class behind it. All three are in the Meeker County Government Center at 114 N Holcombe Avenue, so most errands fit into one visit.

State law fixes the dates, one half before May 16 and the other before October 16. Ask first whether this year's half is paid and whether any older year still shows a balance.

  • Treasurer, Suite 100: 320-693-5345, counter open on weekdays.
  • Auditor, Suite 150: 320-693-5212, for parcel ownership records, rates and special assessments.
  • Assessor: 320-693-5205, for homestead filings and value questions.

Meeker County homes at a glance

Meeker County is in west central Minnesota, with Litchfield as the seat. Other cities include Dassel, Darwin, Cosmos, Cedar Mills, Grove City, Kingston and Watkins, plus part of Eden Valley. The 2020 census counted 23,400 people, and the 2025 estimate is 23,603. About 71.9% of residents lived in rural areas, and 12.4% of the 10,576 housing units were empty in 2020.

There are now 10,969 housing units, and 79.3% of occupied homes are owner occupied. Owner-occupied homes were valued at $249,000 for 2020 to 2024, rent was $904, and only 48 building permits were issued in 2025. Much of the land is rural, so ditches, farmland and lake lots come up often in sales.

How a Meeker County tax bill is built

The Auditor calculates tax capacity rates and then computes tax on roughly 18,000 parcels covering real property, personal property and mobile homes. Rates follow the budgets of the county, townships, cities, school districts and special taxing districts. Special assessments certified by the county, townships and cities are added to the matching parcel and passed through on the same statement.

If you sell farmland or a rural lot, ask about ditches. The Auditor's office keeps the financial records for each county and joint drainage system and files assessments for their upkeep. Once the money comes in, the Treasurer distributes it to the townships, cities, school districts and special districts.

Expect your statement in late March, and a Truth in Taxation notice with next year's estimate in November. Taxes left unpaid for three or more years are subject to forfeiture.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Meeker County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late payment penalties

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets the penalty. Homesteads get the lower rates and nonhomestead parcels pay twice as much.

Late penalty on an unpaid half
WhenHomesteadNonhomestead
Not paid by the deadline2%4%
Open at the start of next month2% more4% more
Every month after, to December1% more1% more
Ceiling8%12%

If the statement was postmarked after April 25, the first deadline moves to 21 days after the postmark. A bill of $100 or less is paid whole at the spring date. Farm homesteads and other qualifying agricultural land can pay the second half through November 15 without penalty. The treasurer takes amounts that differ from the installment, crediting any partial payment to the oldest unpaid one first.

How to pay

Four payment routes are open. Choose whichever fits around your closing.

  • By mail to the Meeker County Treasurer at 114 N Holcombe Avenue, Suite 100, Litchfield, MN 55355, with a postmark no later than the due date. Owners without escrow find a pre-addressed envelope in the statement mailing.
  • Visit the Government Center with cash, a check or a card. Look for the Treasurer just inside the front doors, first office on the right.
  • By credit card, which adds 2.5% to the total, or by e-check at a flat $1.50 through $10,000 and $10 beyond.
  • By direct debit from checking or savings. Print and mail the authorization form, or call 320-693-5345 and ask for the packet.

For escrowed loans the Treasurer sends the figures to the mortgage company, and the lender pays.

How to challenge your valuation

Your first stop is the assessor, and the process climbs from there. Three stages are set by state law, and each one limits the next.

First is the local board, which is your town board or city council. Its meeting falls between April 1 and May 31, and it must wrap up within 20 days. Individual assessments can be trimmed, yet the board cannot lower the assessor's overall total by more than one percent, and exemptions are outside its power. Second is the county board of commissioners and the auditor. It may move a parcel up or down to what it thinks market value is, and an increase requires prior notice and a hearing.

Last comes a petition to district court or Tax Court, filed by April 30 of the payable year. A late notice resets the clock. An owner first told of a change in value, class or exemption status after February 28 of that year gets 60 days from the mailing date to start the appeal. A board cannot grant an individual reduction to an owner who has refused the assessor access to inspect the property.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Meeker County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and refunds when you sell

Who lives in the home decides homestead status, and homestead status decides the penalty rate. New owners should apply right after moving in. You have to buy and occupy by December 1, and the assessor must receive the form by December 15 for it to count the next year. State law asks for Social Security numbers and signatures from every resident owner and from spouses missing from the deed. Only one homestead is allowed per owner, and an approved one stays in place unless the assessor asks for more proof.

Sellers must report a sale or a change of primary residence to the assessor within 30 days. Miss that window and the property can be taxed at its correct class with a penalty equal to the tax. The state also runs a property tax refund tied to income and tax on a principal residence, and Meeker County sends refund questions to the Department of Revenue.

What to check at closing

Three state rules shape the paperwork. Section 272.12 keeps a deed from being recorded until the auditor has checked for delinquent taxes. Section 272.115 asks for a certificate of value on any sale above $3,000, and the seller, the buyer or an agent can file it. Section 272.121 adds a treasurer's certification for deeds that convey only part of a parcel.

Ask the Auditor about ditch assessments on any rural parcel, and ask the Treasurer for a payoff on the current half. The buyer's lender will want both before funding. If the house is inherited or behind on taxes, ask for every open year at once so the payoff matches what the title company will request.

Frequently asked questions

What are the ways to send money to the Meeker County Treasurer?

You can visit, mail a check, pay by card or e-check, or enroll in direct debit. The Treasurer is at 114 N Holcombe Avenue, Suite 100, Litchfield, phone 320-693-5345.

How much is the credit card fee on Meeker County taxes?

A card adds 2.5% of the total. An e-check costs a flat $1.50 up to $10,000 and $10 above.

How steep are late fees on a Meeker County tax half?

On a homestead the penalty is 2%, doubled the next month, then 1% each month to December, stopping at 8%. On other property it is 4%, doubled, then 1% monthly, stopping at 12%.

What is the Meeker County homestead filing cutoff?

The assessor needs the form by December 15, and you must have bought and moved in by December 1. That sets the class for the next year's taxes.

When does unpaid Meeker County tax put a parcel at risk of forfeiture?

Taxes left unpaid for three or more years are subject to forfeiture. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff amount long before then.

Mille Lacs County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota

  • Mille Lacs County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Mille Lacs County, MN Property Tax Guide sale
