Which office does what

Cook County splits the work in two. Value and class are the County Assessor's territory. Statements, payments and delinquent years belong to the Auditor-Treasurer. Their desks are in the courthouse in Grand Marais, at 411 W. 2nd Street.

The Assessor's line is 218-387-3650, for questions on a value, a class, a homestead filing or an inspection visit. The Auditor-Treasurer's line is 218-387-3640, for a statement, a payment or old unpaid years. The county portal accepts current-year payments once amounts are figured in late March. Anything owed from earlier years goes through a phone call instead.

Cook County housing at a glance

Minnesota's far northeastern tip is Cook County, a wooded strip squeezed between Lake Superior and Canada. Roughly 5,522 people share 1,452.57 square miles of land. Grand Marais, Hovland, Grand Portage, Tofte, Schroeder and Lutsen are the named places.

There are 6,251 housing units but only 2,710 households. At the 2020 count, 54.3% of units were empty, a sign of how many cabins and second homes are in the mix. Resident owners occupy 77.7% of lived-in homes, valued at a typical $336,200. The Grand Portage Indian Reservation sits within the county lines.

The buyer pool is small and often seasonal. A lakeshore cabin can carry a tax picture quite unlike a year-round house in town, so read your own statement first and price after.

Due dates and late penalties

Residential and commercial real estate tax splits into May 15 and October 15 installments. Agricultural land gets until November 15 for the second half. If either of this year's halves went unpaid, that balance is already growing.

Under Minnesota Statutes 279.01, a late homestead bill picks up 2% the day after the due date, and a late nonhomestead bill picks up 4%. Further charges land on the first of each following month, stopping at 8% and 12%. For a precise payoff on any year, phone the Auditor-Treasurer.

  • Bills of $100 or less are due in one payment on the first-half date.
  • When the statement missed the April 25 postmark cutoff, the first half falls due 21 days after the mailing date.
  • A check mailed with a postmark within one business day of the deadline qualifies for a single penalty abatement.
  • National Guard and reserve members on federal active duty receive four more months, with orders attached.

Sellers should request a payoff figure dated to the planned closing. Only the county can supply the final number for each parcel.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cook County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Assessment calendar

The Assessor publishes a calendar covering the whole year. Here are the entries that bear on when to list.

Selected Cook County property tax dates
DateWhat happens
January 2Value is set for real and personal property
On or before March 31Statements go out from the Auditor-Treasurer
March to MayMarket value notices arrive from the Assessor, at least 10 days ahead of the local board
April 1 to May 31Local boards hear value complaints
April 30Tax Court petition deadline for current taxes
May 15 and October 15Both halves of real property tax come due
Last 10 meeting days of June after the second FridayCounty board hears appeals
November 24 (on or before)Proposed tax notices go out
December 31Homestead and disabled filings close

Disputing a valuation

Phone the Assessor before anything else. Only if that goes nowhere should you appear before the county's Board of Appeal and Equalization. Presenting to the board takes an appointment, and written comments may be left with the Assessor to be read aloud for you.

  • Gather sales of comparable houses, an appraisal, or contractor quotes proving a defect that is invisible from the street.
  • Phone 218-387-3650 before the board meets, because many disagreements get settled at that counter.
  • Your valuation notice gives the time of the June meeting.
  • If the board keeps the value, the Minnesota Tax Court or the district court is next. Under section 278.01, that petition and its proof of service must be filed by April 30 of the year the bill is due.

State law has the Assessor visit every parcel at least once every five years. The review now underway is tied to the January 2, 2027 assessment and takes in Lutsen, Tofte and Schroeder, with visits scheduled by phone.

Selling with taxes owed

No deed gets recorded while delinquent tax sits on the land. Section 272.12 makes the auditor go through the books and stamp the deed "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered." The recorder turns away any deed lacking that stamp.

Other paperwork rides along with a sale. A price over $3,000 requires a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115). A deed cutting off only a piece of a tax parcel needs a treasurer's certification that the current year's tax on the whole parcel has been paid (section 272.121). Your homestead ends at the sale as well, because the Assessor removes the class for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

Day to day, the title company requests the payoff, takes it from your proceeds and sends the deed on. A cash purchase skips a lender's escrow steps, yet the auditor's review still happens. Find out from the county which years are open on your parcel before agreeing to terms.

A sensible order for a Cook County sale: get a payoff for each open year, confirm your class on the Assessor's roll, line up the certificate of real estate value for the closing agent, and tell the buyer which December 31 homestead filing they will need to make.

Filing cutoffs worth marking

Relief programs run on fixed deadlines. The Assessor must receive a homestead application by December 31 for it to count the next year, and disabled exclusion filings share that date. Blind owners and owners who are permanently and totally disabled have until October 1 for the special homestead class. Requests for a senior citizen deferral are due July 1.

The Property Tax Refund form M-1PR is due August 15. Resorts file a declaration by January 15, and applications for 2c managed forest land are due April 30. The Assessor can say which of these fit your parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Is this the same Cook County as Chicago?

No. This page is about Cook County, Minnesota, along the north shore of Lake Superior, where Grand Marais is the county seat. Property tax questions go to the Assessor at 218-387-3650 or the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640.

When is the next Cook County property tax payment due?

Real estate halves fall on May 15 and October 15 every year, with agricultural land getting until November 15 for its second half. Statements go out on or before March 31. For the amount you owe today, call 218-387-3640.

Can I pay delinquent Cook County taxes online?

No. The portal handles only current-year taxes, and only after amounts are calculated in late March. For earlier years, phone the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 for a payoff on each open year, and raise any partial payment before sending money.

Can I still appeal my Cook County value?

Local boards meet in spring and the county board in June, so call the Assessor at 218-387-3650 to learn where your case stands. A Tax Court or district court petition has to be filed by April 30 of the year the bill is due.

Do I have to pay off the tax before selling a Cook County house?

Delinquent tax has to be cleared first, since the auditor stamps the deed only after that. Call 218-387-3640 for the balance on your parcel while you are still weighing offers.

Which offices handle your tax bill

The Redwood County Government Center, 403 South Mill Street in Redwood Falls, is the single stop. The Assessor (507-637-4008) decides value and class. The Auditor-Treasurer (507-637-4013) sends bills and takes the money. Deeds are filed with the Recorder at 507-637-4032.

Mail goes to P.O. Box 130, Redwood Falls, MN 56283, and the assessor's phone is staffed on weekdays until 4:30 p.m.

Redwood County housing market

This is rolling cropland in southwest Minnesota with Redwood Falls as the seat. The county has 15,265 residents, 1.0% below the 2020 count, and 7,133 housing units. A typical owner-occupied house is worth $158,200. About 78.4% of homes are owner-lived, and median rent is $757 a month. Builders pulled just seven permits in 2025, so resale is most of the market.

The 2020 census found 10.8% of housing units vacant and 21.4% of occupied homes rented. When prices run this low, a small back-tax balance or penalty is a noticeable line on a closing statement.

Due dates

Ordinary real estate pays in mid-May and mid-October. Farm land and manufactured homes pay their second half a month later, and for 2026 that falls on Monday, November 16.

Redwood County property tax due dates for 2026
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateFriday, May 15Thursday, October 15
Agricultural real estateFriday, May 15Monday, November 16
Personal propertyFriday, May 15None
Manufactured homeMonday, August 31Monday, November 16

Section 279.01 of Minnesota Statutes sets the late penalties, with separate rates for homestead and nonhomestead land. Any bounced check, failed electronic payment or reversed payment draws a $30 charge from the county.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Redwood County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Payment options

Pay online through the county's payments page, which includes a parcel lookup, or bring a check or cash to the Government Center, or mail it. A Direct Payment Plan draws from checking or savings, either in two drafts or one yearly draft. Call 507-637-4013 to sign up.

If your lender pays from escrow, read the statement anyway. When a sale is coming, ask this same office for a payoff on the parcel. It also posts the yearly delinquent tax list and the notices for forfeited property sales and sales with unclaimed surplus.

How the assessor arrives at your value

Each parcel is given a class that reflects its use, plus an estimated market value set as of January 2. Under Minnesota Statutes section 273.01 an appraiser visits each property every five years, and tax-exempt parcels every six. Adding a room or a garage can bring a visit sooner.

The annual notice in spring shows that value and class, and it sets the tax for the following year. Details that affect homestead treatment:

  • On January 2 or December 1, the owner or a qualifying relative has to be living there.
  • File the application with the Assessor by December 31 of the assessment year.
  • People who are blind or permanently disabled may apply for a separate class.
  • The homestead exclusion form for disabled owners and the special agricultural homestead forms come from the Assessor's office.

How to contest your valuation

Begin with a call to the assessor about your notice. If that fails, take it to the local board of appeal and equalization for your city or township, which the Assessor's office hosts each April. Most owners have to be heard there before the county board will take the case. That board sits in June in the Commissioner's Room.

Bring proof about your own parcel: a comparable sale, an appraisal, or photos of a defect. Keep the discussion on the value and class of your parcel, since the boards cannot change the tax rate or the bill itself. A written summary of your points, handed to the clerk at the meeting, helps the members follow your case. If you plan to sell soon, an appraisal you paid for anyway can double as evidence. Beyond the boards, a petition to district court or Tax Court under section 278.01 is the last route, and it has an April 30 filing date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Redwood County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with tax still owing

Any tax still open in early January is delinquent under section 279.02, and 2% is added at once. Closing brings a second issue. Under section 272.12 the auditor has to stamp the deed with a no-delinquent-tax note before the Recorder will take it, with exceptions that include probate distribution deeds and transfer on death deeds.

Usually the title agent deducts the balance from your proceeds. Phone the Auditor-Treasurer ahead of time so the figure on the closing statement holds no surprises. Cash sales follow the same rule and only skip the lender escrow payoff.

Recording tools to use before a sale

The Recorder offers three. LandShark is a web tool for searching land records and viewing document images, and an account needs a signed web portal agreement with an original wet signature plus a set-up fee. Land Notification emails you when anything is filed against your personal or business name, so a surprise lien shows up quickly. Sign up before you list, because a lien you did not know about can stall a closing for weeks. The eCRV tool is where the sale certificate gets filed, and paper certificates have not been accepted for sales since October 1, 2014.

After closing, the assessor drops homestead classification on the sold property for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies, under section 272.115.

A seller's checklist

Taxes come up at several points in a sale. Go through this list before you take an offer.

  1. Find your parcel on the county's online payments page and note which halves are paid.
  2. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 for a payoff figure, and ask whether any special assessment is attached to the parcel.
  3. Check the class on your spring notice with the Assessor at 507-637-4008. If you never filed for homestead, the deadline is December 31 of the assessment year.
  4. Hand the payoff figure to your title agent so the amount is deducted at closing. Ask for the figure in writing and keep a copy with your closing papers.
  5. Make sure the sale certificate is filed electronically, since paper certificates are not taken.
  6. Tell the buyer that homestead status does not carry over. The new owner has to apply.

A cash buyer makes the list shorter, since no lender escrow account needs settling. The tax still has to be clear and the sale certificate filed before the deed can be recorded.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the last Redwood County tax deadline of the year?

It is the second half on farm land and manufactured homes, due in mid-November. For 2026 the date is Monday, November 16. Standard real estate second halves are due October 15.

Who can I call about a Redwood County home value I think is too high?

Ring the County Assessor at 507-637-4008. Still unhappy? Go to the local board in April, then the county board in June.

Can a Redwood County house be sold with property tax still owing?

Yes, as long as the balance is cleared before the Recorder files the deed. It usually comes out of the seller's proceeds. The Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 can give the exact payoff.

What is the Redwood County homestead application deadline?

The deadline is December 31 of the assessment year. Either the owner or a qualifying relative must live in the home on January 2 or December 1.

Will the buyer automatically get my Redwood County homestead status?

No. Once the deed transfers, the assessor takes homestead off for the next assessment year unless the new owner applies and qualifies.

Who to contact about property tax in Swift County

The Auditor-Treasurer's Office in the courthouse at 301 14th Street North in Benson handles bills and payments, and the Assessor handles value and class. Mail goes to P.O. Box 207, Benson, MN 56215. The office phone is 320-843-4069, and the Treasurer's line for the online tax search is 320-843-3544.

The county Assessor page explains an unusual split. The 21 townships contract with local assessors, while the eight cities and villages contract with the County Assessor. A rural seller may therefore be dealing with a township assessor, and a seller in Benson or Appleton with the county office. Your valuation notice or the county can tell you which assessor set your value.

The Auditor-Treasurer also keeps tax forfeiture sale listings, takes automatic withdrawal forms and posts a real estate tax search. Swift County's Land Records Office, which files deeds, is a separate counter in the same courthouse.

Housing in Swift County

Swift is a quiet farm county in west central Minnesota with Benson as its seat and largest city. About 9,800 people live there (9,763 in July 2025, down 0.7% since April 2020). The county has 4,727 housing units, owners occupy 72.4%, the median owner-occupied value is $161,400 and median gross rent is $920. Only 34 building permits were issued in 2025. The median is only a midpoint for homes that vary widely between town lots and farmsteads.

How a Swift County homestead gets approved

You must own and live in the home by December 1 and file the application by December 15. Applications are available at the Assessor's Office. Without a homestead classification the property is taxed at a nonhomestead rate, which also means a higher late penalty under Minnesota Statutes 279.01.

For a city parcel, the county assessor does the following:

  • Finds and lists taxable property and sets its use and classification.
  • Estimates market value by studying sales and mails the owner a notice each year.
  • Decides which parcels qualify for homestead.
  • Gives realtors, appraisers and others public information on request.

A bill can change because of township, city, school or county budgets, voter-approved school levies, special assessments such as ditch, sewer and street projects, and changes made by the Minnesota Legislature.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Swift County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and late penalties

The first half is due May 15 and the second half on October 15, with agricultural land given until November 15. The automatic withdrawal form uses those three dates, and Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets them.

A half that misses its date gets a 2 percent penalty on homestead property or 4 percent on nonhomestead property, with more added on the first of each following month. A tract with taxes of $100 or less owes the full amount with the first half. The treasurer must abate a late penalty one time if the payment is postmarked within one business day of the due date.

The tax search can be reached from the real estate taxes page. If it will not load, call the Treasurer's Office at 320-843-3544. A delinquency notice costs $10 per parcel for publication under the county fee schedule, and a Confession of Judgment payment plan is $250 per parcel, so catching up before the notice is worth the effort. A tax search on one parcel costs $2. Partial payments are accepted, so an owner who cannot pay a full half on the due date can still reduce what accrues.

Selling with taxes owed

Pay what you can and call the courthouse, because Minnesota lets the county treasurer take a partial payment and apply it to the oldest unpaid installment first. Any shortfall is then charged to penalty before tax. The Auditor-Treasurer's Office at 320-843-4069 can state the exact payoff, including accrued penalty and any publication charge.

The county keeps a page titled Taxes, Delinquent and Forfeiture, and forfeiture sale listings are handled at that same number. A seller who is behind should settle the balance, or arrange a payment plan, before a closing date is set. A cash buyer or a title company will ask for the same payoff figure, so get it in writing early and plan to clear it from the proceeds at closing.

Steps before you list a Swift County home

  1. Find out who assessed the property. A township parcel goes through a local assessor, while a parcel in one of the eight cities goes through the County Assessor. Your valuation notice or the county can tell you which.
  2. Look up the parcel in the online real estate tax search, or call the Treasurer's Office at 320-843-3544 if the search will not load.
  3. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 320-843-4069 for the exact payoff, including accrued penalty and any publication charge, so there are no surprises at the table.
  4. Check that the homestead classification is in place. A parcel that missed the December 15 filing is taxed at the nonhomestead rate, and a late half costs more.
  5. For acreage, ask about the zoning district and any feedlot or ditch record, since buyers of rural land tend to ask.
  6. Before the deed is prepared, ask Land Records whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens.

None of these steps takes long, and together they head off most of the questions that stall a closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Swift County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording costs for a Swift County deed or sale

The county fee schedule lists the recording costs, and the largest is the deed tax. The state-set deed tax is the purchase price times 0.0033, and a mortgage registration tax is the loan amount times 0.0023.

Swift County Land Records fees
Document or serviceFee
Well disclosure certificate$54
Plat$56
State tax lien release$30
Certified copy$10
Attested copy$2
Torrens original certificate of title$46

Land Records is also the Registrar of Titles for Torrens property, which is registered land, and the Registrar must check documents before issuing a certificate of title. County records go back to the 1870s, and Minnesota's race-notice rule means the first to record gains priority. If a deed is going on, file it promptly and ask whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens before you prepare it.

Local permits that might affect a Swift County sale

Rural parcels can involve county zoning permits, and the fee schedule posts them. A dwelling, addition, mobile home or cabin permit is $50, a sewage permit $100, a variance $250 and a conditional use permit $500. The E911 address fee is $151. These costs matter if a buyer plans to build, add on or change the use of land.

Environmental Services issues the permits, and applications and feedlot reports are filed under that department. Buyers who plan to build or add on will want the permit costs up front, so share this list early. Ask for the zoning district and any feedlot or ditch record when you list acreage.

Frequently asked questions

What is the phone number for the Swift County Auditor-Treasurer?

320-843-4069 for the Auditor-Treasurer, and 320-843-3544 for the Treasurer's Office. Both are at the courthouse, 301 14th Street North, Benson.

When is the Swift County homestead deadline?

You must own and occupy the home by December 1 and apply by December 15. The Assessor's Office has the application.

Which Swift County cities use the county assessor?

The eight cities and villages: Appleton, Benson, Clontarf, Danvers, De Graff, Holloway, Kerkhoven and Murdock. The 21 townships use local assessors.

How much is Minnesota deed tax in Swift County?

Deed tax is the purchase price times 0.0033. A well disclosure certificate adds $54 when one is needed.

Does Swift County offer automatic tax withdrawals?

Yes. The Auditor-Treasurer posts an automatic withdrawal form that draws on May 15, October 15 for nonagricultural parcels and November 15 for agricultural parcels.

Nobles County payment calendar for the 2026 tax year
Due dateProperty and installment
May 15, 2026All taxes, first half
August 31, 2026Mobile home taxes, first half
October 15, 2026City taxes, second half, if applicable
November 16, 2026Farm taxes and mobile home taxes, second half, if applicable

The second half is not mailed, so keep the first-half stub. The county processes payments within 24 hours of receipt. If you are late, call the office at 507-295-5258 to learn the penalty to include. The state sets it under section 279.01: 2% on homestead and 4% on other property for the first missed date, rising monthly to caps of 8% and 12%.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Nobles County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to pay

The county offers six methods:

  • Mail a check payable to Nobles County Auditor-Treasurer with the stub from every parcel; the postmark must be on or before the due date
  • Direct payment plan, which pulls the amount from a checking or savings account until you cancel
  • Online by card or e-check, with convenience fees
  • In person at the Government Center by check, cash or card
  • The drop box outside the main entrance on the 10th Street side, open around the clock
  • Escrow through a mortgage lender, which applies when the lender's name appears at the top of the statement

The county will not take post-dated checks, and a private postage meter mark does not prove timely mailing. Liability for the tax stands even if a statement never arrives.

How to contest your valuation

Only the estimated market value for the current assessment year can be contested, and the number is struck as of January 2. The board reviews the value and class behind your bill, not the tax amount. Call the Assessor first to check the facts on your notice.

  1. Go to your local board, or the open book session if your area holds one. Valuation notices must be mailed at least 10 days beforehand.
  2. If the result still looks wrong, take it to the County Board of Equalization. It meets in June after the second Friday and may sit up to 10 consecutive meeting days. Recent meetings started at 6:00 PM.
  3. File with the Minnesota Tax Court or district court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, under section 278.01.

Neither board can grant special program status, such as Green Acres. Those need their own application, and a board may not give relief to an owner who refused the assessor entry to inspect.

Before closing on a Nobles County sale

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for any balance on the parcel, since delinquent tax and unpaid special assessments surface at transfer. Under section 272.12, the auditor looks up delinquent tax when a deed arrives, and the recorder refuses a deed lacking the "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" stamp.

The office handles tax forfeiture proceedings, and its property tax page links to a list of tax forfeiture property. Selling well ahead of that stage keeps the decision with you.

If your lender collects through escrow, ask the lender how the escrow balance will be handled at payoff, and ask the Auditor-Treasurer whether the second half has been paid. Bring the parcel number and your closing date to the call. A buyer paying cash has no escrow to reconcile, but the same stamp is still needed before the deed can be recorded.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Nobles County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps for a seller, in order

A short checklist keeps the tax side of a sale from becoming a closing-day problem.

  1. Pull the latest statement and confirm which payments have been made. If a lender pays through escrow, the lender's name appears at the top.
  2. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-295-5258 and ask for the current balance, including any special assessments or ditch fund charges on the parcel.
  3. Check your property class with the Assessor. A homestead form that was never filed can leave you with a higher bill than you expected.
  4. Tell your title company about any open balance so it can be paid from the sale proceeds.
  5. Keep the first-half stub and the receipt for each payment. The second half is not mailed, and a receipt settles any later question about what was paid.

A buyer who pays cash and closes quickly still needs the county to mark the deed, so a clean balance saves the most time. Contact the office early if your parcel includes farm land, because those taxes follow a different second-half date than city property.

Frequently asked questions

What is the phone number for Nobles County property taxes?

Call 507-295-5258 for the Auditor-Treasurer, who collects tax. The Assessor, who sets value and class, is at 507-295-5208. Both are in the Government Center at 315 Tenth Street, Worthington.

Why is the farm tax date sometimes November 16?

The usual agricultural date of November 15 lands on a Sunday in some years. When that happens, the deadline for farm and mobile home second-half payments moves to Monday, November 16.

Does Nobles County mail second-half tax statements?

No. The county does not mail second-half statements, so you must keep the stub from the first mailing. Taxpayers remain responsible for payment even when no statement reaches them.

Can I use the drop box for a late-night payment?

Yes. The drop box outside the Government Center's main entrance on 10th Street is accessible 24 hours a day. A mailed payment instead needs a postmark on or before the due date.

Can I appeal a Nobles County tax bill amount?

You can contest the estimated market value or classification, not the tax amount itself. Start with the Assessor, then the local board or open book, then the County Board, and file any Tax Court petition by April 30.

Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Douglas County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Douglas County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Douglas County?
We buy Douglas County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Who handles property tax

The work is shared by two offices in Alexandria. The Assessor's Office values and classifies about 30,000 parcels. The Auditor/Treasurer calculates, bills and collects the tax. County hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Assessor: 305 8th Avenue West, 2nd floor, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3884, email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us.
  • Auditor/Treasurer: 821 Cedar Street, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3077, tax email taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us.

The county's Parcel Info Lookup brings up the tax statement and the value notice for a parcel. Some assessment districts hire their own local assessor under contract, so phone the county office if you want to know who actually viewed your house.

Selling in lake country

Douglas County is lake country in west-central Minnesota, with Alexandria as both seat and largest city. About 83 of its 720 square miles are water, spread over more than 250 lakes. Other cities include Brandon, Carlos, Evansville, Forada, Garfield, Kensington, Millerville, Miltona, Nelson and part of Osakis.

Roughly 40,120 people live here in 17,519 households. The county has 23,040 housing units, and the median owner-occupied value is $321,400. Owners live in 76.5 percent of occupied homes, and median household income is $79,043. At the 2020 count, 23.9 percent of housing units were vacant, a number that can include seasonal lake homes.

That vacancy figure matters because the assessor classifies seasonal residential property separately from year-round homes. Know which class your house sits in before you set a price.

Payment dates

Real estate tax comes due in two halves, May 15 and October 15, and the postmark counts. Agricultural property and mobile homes have a later second-half date of November 15, and mobile home first-half tax is due August 31.

A missed deadline brings a 2 percent penalty on homestead and 4 percent on non-homestead property (Minn. Stat. 279.01).

Douglas County tax payment dates
Tax typeFirst paymentSecond payment
Real estateMay 15October 15
AgriculturalMay 15November 15
Mobile homeAugust 31November 15
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Douglas County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to pay

Five choices are on offer from the Auditor/Treasurer: an ACH direct payment plan, a drop box, online credit card or virtual check, mail, or a visit to the office. The office has moved from the courthouse to the Administration Building, so head to the Administration Building, not the courthouse.

  • Drop boxes: one on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot, both at 821 Cedar Street.
  • Online: reached from the county website through the parcel lookup.
  • ACH: the direct payment plan debits your account on the due dates.

For a duplicate statement by mail, call 320-762-3077. For a copy of the value notice, call the assessor at 320-762-3884.

How values are set

Values are fixed as of January 2 each year, and sales do most of the work. The assessor compares sale prices with assessed values to test each district against state standards, then mails every owner a notice of value and classification in the spring. Property falls into five classes: residential, seasonal, apartment, agricultural and commercial/industrial. Each property is also either homestead or non-homestead.

A higher value does not by itself raise your bill. Your taxable market value is multiplied by the class rate to find your share of the levy set by the county, the city or township and the school district.

The assessor's FAQ explains what does and does not push value up. Minor repairs such as a new roof, porch repair, original siding, paint or replaced plumbing and electrical fixtures usually will not raise the estimated market value alone, though several together could. Report fire or storm damage, since the assessment date is January 2.

Appealing an assessment

Phone the assessor first at 320-762-3884. Formal appeals follow an order, and the June county board hears you only if the local board or open book meeting did first.

  1. Local board or open book. These run in April by appointment. Your valuation notice names the date and place for your district, and Alexandria has its own city board.
  2. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. This meets in June.
  3. Minnesota Tax Court. The petition is filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Meetings cannot change the statement you are paying now. They affect only the next one. Owners who struggle with a homestead bill can look at the state Department of Revenue's M1PR form, which sets income against property tax due and may produce a partial refund.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Douglas County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Qualifying for homestead

To qualify, occupy the property as your primary residence, be an owner or a relative of an owner, and be a Minnesota resident. Voter registration, driver's license, income tax forms and vehicle registration should all show the homestead address.

Check this before a sale in a lake county. A cottage a family treats as a second home is seasonal class, and the class rate differs from a year-round homestead. If the buyer plans to live in the house, the assessor needs a fresh application from them, so hand the buyer the assessor's number, 320-762-3884, early.

Moving also means updating the mailing address on the tax record. A Taxpayer Address Change Request Form can be emailed or mailed to the Auditor-Treasurer's Office at 821 Cedar Street, so the next statement reaches the right owner.

Tax at the closing table

The county auditor must see that no delinquent tax sits on the land before a deed can be recorded (Minn. Stat. 272.12). Request the tax payoff from the closing agent before the signing date, and ask how the current half-year is divided between you and the buyer under your purchase agreement.

Every new homestead needs an application, so buyers who want the class must apply. An owner who lives in the house but is not getting homestead status should contact the assessor. Taxes left unpaid long enough can end in forfeiture. Forfeited property goes to the state after the redemption period ends, and that period has been three years since January 1, 2014, down from five.

A cash buyer skips lender escrow, but the county's delinquency check still applies. Gather your parcel number, confirm both halves are paid, and ask the Auditor/Treasurer for the payoff in writing. Having these in hand a week before closing keeps the title company from waiting on county answers.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Douglas County Auditor/Treasurer's phone number?

The office number is 320-762-3077, at 821 Cedar Street in Alexandria. Tax questions can also go to taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us, and hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Can I pay Douglas County property tax by drop box?

Yes. There is a box on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot. Mailed payments count as timely by postmark.

Do I need an appointment to appeal a Douglas County value?

Yes, local board and open book meetings are by appointment. Call the assessor at 320-762-3884 or email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us, and call the city if you live in Alexandria and want its board.

What is the November tax notice from Douglas County?

It is the proposed tax notice for the next year, mailed in mid to late November. It is separate from the statement you receive by March 31.

How long do I have to redeem a Douglas County parcel that went tax forfeit?

The redemption period is three years, shortened from five years effective January 1, 2014. Contact the Auditor/Treasurer at 320-762-3077 before that period ends.

Offices and phone numbers

Both offices are in the courthouse at 101 Fillmore Street in Preston, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Auditor/Treasurer's Office stays open through the noon hour.

  • Auditor/Treasurer: PO Box 627, Preston, MN 55965. Phone 507-765-3811 or 507-765-4701. Email auditor@fillmorecountymn.gov.
  • Assessor: PO Box 466, Preston, MN 55965. Phone 507-765-3868. Allow two business days for an email reply.

The Auditor/Treasurer keeps the tax roll, so ownership changes, splits, combinations and transfers all pass through that desk. The same office prepares the property tax statements and runs the county's tax-forfeited land sales. A property tax search and statement lookup is available through the Beacon site linked from the county page.

What Fillmore County is like for a seller

Fillmore County lies along the Iowa border in the southeastern corner of Minnesota, in the Driftless Area, and belongs to the Rochester metropolitan area. Preston is the county seat and Spring Valley is the largest city. Rolling hills, gullies and karst shape most parcels, and the Root River drains the county eastward. Cities include Canton, Chatfield (part), Fountain, Harmony, Lanesboro, Mabel, Ostrander, Peterson, Rushford, Rushford Village, Wykoff and Whalan.

About 21,540 people live here, and 92.5 percent stayed in the same house for a year, so owners tend to hold on for long stretches. The county has 9,890 housing units and 8,723 households. Owners occupy 82.6 percent of occupied homes, with a median value of $221,100, and median household income is $77,512. Only 58 building permits were issued in 2025, so new supply is thin.

Median monthly owner costs run $1,520 with a mortgage and $588 without one. Even a paid-off house carries a steady monthly bill, and a family holding an inherited house for a few months still pays it. Get the tax figure early and plan around it.

Due dates and late penalties

Two installments, mid-May and mid-October, cover residential real estate. Minn. Stat. 279.01 puts the first half due before May 16 and the second before October 16. Farm and mobile home owners have until November 15 for their second half.

Weekends can move the date, so check the one printed on your statement rather than relying on a fixed day. A late payment draws 2 percent on homestead and 4 percent on non-homestead the day after, and the penalty grows each month after that.

Fillmore County payment timing
Payment or filingWhen

Automatic payments

The Auditor/Treasurer runs a no-charge ACH service that pulls property tax from a checking or savings account on the due dates. It helps you avoid late fees caused by postal delays. Call 507-765-3811 or write to the auditor email above to sign up.

When the house sells, cancel or update the ACH authorization so the old account is not debited for a bill that belongs to the buyer. Ask the office how long a change takes before the next due date.

How an appeal works

Phone the assessor at 507-765-3868 first. The valuation notice lists the formal options and the dates for your township or city, and it is the only place those dates are fixed for the year.

  1. Talk to the assessor. Value changes usually come from appraisal work in your jurisdiction or from market adjustments that bring assessment statistics into range.
  2. Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, or open book. If the call does not settle things, this is the first formal step. State law keeps these meetings between April 1 and May 31 (Minn. Stat. 274.01).
  3. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. Contact the assessor ahead of the June meeting to be put on the agenda. The board meets in the commissioners' board room at the courthouse.
  4. Minnesota Tax Court. If those steps fail, the petition is due April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Once the county board adjourns very few options remain, so bring written supporting documents. If you refuse the assessor access to the inside of the house, a board cannot give you a value or class change that benefits the property (Minn. Stat. 274.01).

Before closing on a Fillmore County house

Have the title agent run delinquent tax before the deed goes to the auditor. The auditor checks the land for delinquent tax and certifies it, and the recorder may not take the deed without that certificate (Minn. Stat. 272.12).

Much of the county is farmland, so also check whether the parcel is being split or combined, since the auditor maintains those records. Farm owners get a later second-half date. A farm sale closing between October 15 and November 15 can leave a half-year of tax open even though no penalty has started, so ask the closing agent and the auditor which half is outstanding.

The usual sequence: look up the parcel on Beacon, confirm both halves, request the payoff for the closing date, cancel any ACH debit, and give the buyer the assessor's number if they want to file for homestead.

Tax that goes unpaid

The Auditor/Treasurer conducts the county's tax-forfeited land sales, which is where a parcel ends up when its tax stays unpaid.

If you inherited a house or are behind, call the auditor at 507-765-3811 for the full balance with penalty and interest and for the parcel's status. The treasurer applies any payment to the oldest unpaid installment first (Minn. Stat. 279.01), so a partial payment reduces the oldest year before the current one.

Selling an inherited or farm parcel

Inherited houses and farm parcels raise the same few questions. Is a split or combination pending? Which half-year is still open? The Auditor/Treasurer can answer all three from one desk, and the answers are best known before you list.

Plan your timeline around the due dates. A house that closes in early summer has the first half already due, while one that closes in late fall may have only the second half left. Whichever it is, the purchase agreement decides how the year is divided between buyer and seller, and the title agent will want the payoff figure in writing. If a parcel is behind, paying the oldest year first clears the way for the deed to be certified.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Fillmore County Auditor/Treasurer located?

The office is at 101 Fillmore Street in Preston, MN 55965, with mail going to PO Box 627. The phone numbers are 507-765-3811 and 507-765-4701.

Does Fillmore County offer automatic tax payments?

Yes. A no-charge ACH service takes the payment from a checking or savings account on the due dates. Call 507-765-3811 to enroll.

Who do I call about my Fillmore County property value?

Call the Assessor at 507-765-3868. Allow two business days for an email response, and use the valuation notice you receive to see the next formal appeal steps.

When is the second half due for a Fillmore County farm?

November 15 for agricultural property and mobile homes. Regular residential real estate is due October 15.

Can I search my Fillmore County tax statement online?

Yes. The Auditor/Treasurer page links to a property tax search and statement lookup on the Beacon site.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Le Sueur County?

Who handles property tax in Le Sueur County

Value and class come from the Assessor. The tax itself is figured and collected by the Auditor-Treasurer. The Assessor's office is at 88 S Park Avenue, Le Center, MN 56057, phone 507-357-8213.

The staff covers about 19,000 parcels in 14 townships and 10 cities. Their work is estimating market value, sorting property by its main use (residential, agricultural, seasonal or commercial) and ruling on which parcels get homestead. Each year a sales study compares assessed values to real sales, and the Minnesota Department of Revenue expects the estimate to land between 90% and 105% of actual market value.

On the billing side, each taxing district certifies its levy, and the Auditor-Treasurer converts those levies into a bill using the Assessor's values and the state's classifications. The same office processes real estate transactions for property in the county.

Le Sueur County market snapshot

Along the Minnesota River in south central Minnesota, Le Sueur County is counted in the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metro area. It had 29,453 residents in July 2025, a 2.8% gain on the 28,663 of 2020. There are 13,256 housing units, and 81.0% of occupied homes are owner occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $316,500, and median household income is $94,968.

The county is largely rural, with 85.8% of residents outside urban areas in 2020. Cities include Le Center (the seat), Le Sueur, Montgomery, Waterville, Elysian, New Prague, Cleveland, Kasota, Kilkenny and Heidelberg. Agricultural, seasonal and residential are separate classes, so a lake or farm parcel can be taxed differently from a house in town, and the Assessor sets the class on acreage and farmland by how it is used.

How to pay your bill

Accepted payment types are cash, check, money order, card and ACH. A third-party processor runs card payments and adds a 2.5% convenience fee.

The county's Beacon mapping application lets you look up a property, view a map and pay taxes online. Beacon also has subscription services for name searches and comparable property searches. A single-family property tax calculator spreadsheet, certified tax rates for 2025 and 2026, and levy history sit on the Property Tax Info page, so you can see how much of a bill comes from each taxing district before you list.

The due dates printed on your statement are the ones that count, and the state rule is summarized in the next section.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Le Sueur County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

State law divides a bill over $100 into a spring half, due before May 16, and a fall half, due before October 16. A bill of $100 or less is paid whole at the spring date.

How the penalty grows (Minnesota Statutes 279.01)
StepHomesteadNonhomestead
Not paid by the due date2%4%
Still open on the 1st of next monthAdditional 2%Additional 4%
Every month after, to December1% more1% more

A statement mailed after April 24 pushes the first-half deadline to 21 days after its postmark, and penalties run from that later date.

How a valuation appeal works

Every March the Assessor sends each owner a valuation notice that names the local Board of Appeal and Equalization, the place to object. Meeting dates are posted on the county's schedule page, and your notice gives the time and location.

Going to court means following section 278.01 of Minnesota Statutes: serve a petition on the county auditor and file it with the district court administrator by April 30 of the payable year. Tax Court is the alternative, and its appeal opens when the notice lands and closes the day before May 1. Before filing, check with the Auditor-Treasurer on whether you must make a minimum payment.

Reading your statement and the county's tools

Start with the parcel number, since every lookup in the county's systems runs through it. The statement shows what each taxing district asked for, and the certified tax rates for 2025 and 2026 posted on the Property Tax Info page let you check those figures against the county's own list. The levy history on the same page shows how each district's request has moved, which helps explain why a bill went up even when your value did not.

If you want to see how a comparable house is treated, Beacon's property search lets you look at neighboring parcels and their maps. Pairing that with the assessor's yearly sales study is a reasonable way to judge whether your value is in line before the March notice arrives. The Department of Revenue expects assessed values to sit between 90% and 105% of actual market value, so a number far outside that range is worth a call to 507-357-8213.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Le Sueur County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Relief for homeowners

Homeowners whose tax is high compared with household income may get a state property tax refund, the first item on the county's Property Tax Info page. Claims are due August 15 with the Department of Revenue, and late ones are taken for a year.

The Assessor decides which parcels qualify for homestead classification, and as the penalty table shows, homestead owners start at a lower rate. If you have moved out or the house is empty after an estate, ask the Assessor whether the homestead status ends and when.

What closing looks like on the tax side

On closing day the tax work comes down to three numbers: what you owe for the current year through the day you hand over the keys, any special assessment balance, and any penalty on an old installment. Your title company will ask the county for these. Giving the Auditor-Treasurer your parcel number and expected closing date ahead of time lets them quote an exact payoff instead of an estimate.

When both halves of the year are already paid, there is little left to do except agree with the buyer on how the year is divided. When a half is open, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at the table. Either way, the buyer has to apply for homestead on their own if they plan to live in the house, since the seller's status does not transfer by itself.

Checklist before selling a Le Sueur County house

Confirm both halves of the current year are paid, get the parcel's special assessment balance, and compare the next due date with your closing date. The Auditor-Treasurer's office handles real estate transactions, so a stop there before closing keeps surprises off the settlement statement.

Bring the parcel number, your latest statement and the date you hope to close, and let the office give you the amount to pay through that date. Ask the Assessor to confirm the parcel's class too. A lake lot or acreage can sit in a different class than the house beside it, and a buyer's lender may ask about it.

If the property is inherited or has been empty, add one more question: whether any older year is open. Settle that first, because a payoff that leaves an earlier year out will surface again at the title company, and a cash sale does not remove the need to clear it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Le Sueur County Assessor's address?

88 S Park Avenue, Le Center, MN 56057, phone 507-357-8213. Le Center is also the county seat.

Does Le Sueur County charge a fee for card payments?

Yes. A 2.5% convenience fee is added when a credit or debit card is run. Cash, check, money order and ACH are also accepted.

When does the Le Sueur County board of appeal meet?

It meets once a year, with the date and time printed on your March valuation notice and posted on the county's schedule page. Notices for the next year go out each March.

Can I file for the state property tax refund after August 15?

Yes, for up to one year after the due date, which is August 15.

Freeborn County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Freeborn County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Freeborn County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Freeborn County?
We buy Freeborn County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who runs property tax

Both offices sit in the Freeborn County Government Center at 411 Broadway South in Albert Lea. Mail goes to PO Box 1147, Albert Lea, MN 56007. The Assessor values and classifies property. The Auditor-Treasurer computes and collects the tax.

  • Assessor: 507-377-5176. Open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Auditor-Treasurer: 507-377-5117 for taxes and the real estate drop box.

Freeborn runs a true county assessor system, so the county assesses every parcel, including those in small cities and townships. The auditor's office keeps records, transfer cards, tax maps and certificates of value on about 22,000 parcels, and it records changes such as transfers, sales, splits and mortgages. It also collects special assessments for cities and townships and passes them on.

Freeborn County housing for sellers

Freeborn County is on Minnesota's southern border with Iowa. Albert Lea is both seat and largest city, and the county forms the Albert Lea micropolitan area. The Shell Rock River flows south out of Albert Lea Lake toward Iowa, and Myre-Big Island State Park is inside the county.

About 30,440 people live here. The median owner-occupied value is $171,100, owners occupy 79.5 percent of occupied homes, and median household income is $71,023. Median gross rent is $849. The county has 14,114 housing units, with 7.4 percent vacant at the 2020 count, and issued only 13 building permits in 2025.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,316, and owners without one report $563. About one in four residents is 65 or older, and 90.0 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. Estate sales and long-held homes are a regular part of the Albert Lea market.

Payment dates and fees

The two real estate installments fall in May and October. Minnesota's statute requires payment before May 16 and before October 16, and agricultural property has until November 15 for the second half. A missed date adds 2 percent for homestead or 4 percent for non-homestead (Minn. Stat. 279.01), then another 1 percent each month through December.

Online payments made before midnight on the due date are credited to that day. The credit can take up to four working days to show on the county's Beacon tax site, so keep your confirmation.

Payment methodCost or detail

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Freeborn County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The 2027 reassessment and your sale

It can affect you. The Assessor's Office has appraisers visiting properties to photograph them and verify characteristics for the 2027 assessment, which sets property taxes payable in 2028. Minnesota requires a physical inspection at least once every five years.

The review covers Albert Lea residential property, the small cities of Clarks Grove, Glenville, Manchester and Myrtle, and the townships of Hayward, Manchester, Moscow, Oakland and Pickerel Lake. Appraisers drive county vehicles, wear safety vests and carry badges, and postcards go to owners before the visit. They may ask to see the inside of the house.

You may decline, but there is a cost. An owner can refuse in person or in writing, and the assessor then estimates interior condition by assumption. Under Minn. Stat. 274.13, a board may not grant a value or class change to a property whose owner refused inspection. Refusing does not stop you from attending the board of appeal and equalization.

How values are set

The assessor estimates what a property would likely sell for on the open market. State standards require values between 90 and 105 percent of market value, measured from a sample of sales rather than any one sale. The county analyzes sales to build a formula, applies it to all properties, and tests the result against statistical requirements.

The Assessor posts annual sales reports covering Albert Lea residential sales, small city residential, township residential, duplexes and triplexes, rural residential land, vacant land and agricultural sales. Reading the report for your category is a quick way to see whether your value is in line before you list.

  • Market trends, interest rates, local economic conditions and supply all feed into value.
  • A higher tax bill does not always mean a higher value. Local government spending, school bonds, legislative changes and new construction in the county also move the bill.

Owing back tax

Use the county's delinquent tax list and watch its "Interest Figured To" date. Interest rises on the first of each month, so the figure shown ages quickly, and the county posts an updated list in the first week of each month. Call the auditor at 507-377-5117 for an exact payoff.

When a parcel has several delinquent years and you cannot pay them all, the county's rule is to pay the most recent year first. Delinquent real property taxes are applied in inverse order, starting with the latest year. Plan to clear the full balance before closing, because the county auditor checks for delinquent tax before it enters a transfer on the books (Minn. Stat. 272.12).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Freeborn County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appealing a valuation

Call the assessor at 507-377-5176 when your notice arrives. If talking does not help, the local board of appeal and equalization hears the first formal appeal in April or May (Minn. Stat. 274.01), then the county board in June. The last stop is the Minnesota Tax Court, with a petition due April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Bring comparable sales and photographs, not a general complaint about the bill. A bill can rise for reasons other than your value, including local spending and school bonds, and a valuation appeal cannot reverse any of those.

Getting ready to close

A short checklist helps a Freeborn sale go smoothly. Look up the parcel on the Beacon site, confirm both installments are paid, and check the delinquent list for older years. Call 507-377-5117 for the payoff on your closing date. If appraisers have visited recently, keep the photos or notes from that visit, since they show what the county recorded about the house. Tell the buyer which homestead filing, if any, they will need, and send them to the Assessor at 507-377-5176 for the form. The sale does not stop the county from billing the parcel, so the statement that arrives next March may still carry your name until the transfer is entered. Ask the auditor how long that entry takes.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Freeborn County Assessor's phone number?

It is 507-377-5176, at 411 Broadway South in Albert Lea. The Assessor's Office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

How much does it cost to pay Freeborn County tax by card?

Card payments from $0 to $60 cost $2.00, and payments of $61 or more cost 2.35 percent. An e-check carries a flat $2.00 fee.

Is there a drop box for Freeborn County property tax?

Yes. The Real Estate Taxes Drop Off box sits inside the Law Enforcement entrance of the Freeborn County Government Center. Call 507-377-5117 if you need help.

Which Freeborn County areas are being reassessed for 2027?

Albert Lea residential property, the small cities of Clarks Grove, Glenville, Manchester and Myrtle, and the townships of Hayward, Manchester, Moscow, Oakland and Pickerel Lake.

Which delinquent year do I pay first in Freeborn County?

The most recent delinquent year. Delinquent real property tax is paid in inverse order, so a partial payment goes against the latest year first.
